articles.title: CTTI is Exponential, RTTI is Linear
articles.summary: Runtime Type Information (RTTI) has a linear cost in the number of types it requires, with a single cost for iterating over the types in the table. This is in contrast to Compile-Time Type Information (CTTI), which is an exponential cost due to the need to create tables for each type. The cost of RTTI is spread across procedures, tables, and semantic checking, making it a fixed constant cost. In contrast, CTTI can be an exponential cost due to the need to create tables for each type, but the cost is not necessarily linear.

articles.title: Let's build a compressor from scratch

This approach can be used to compress a wide range of data types, including text files, software binaries, and even audio and video files.

articles.summary: The browser's main thread is expensive due to its heavy workload of running JavaScript, event handlers, timers, network response callbacks, and the framework's internals, which all execute in a seemingly unrelated order to screen refresh cycles. This expensive resource handling can cause stuttering, button delays, and other jank issues, even if the code itself is not slow. To handle this, developers can split tasks into two categories: running JavaScript and drawing the screen, and use techniques like requestAnimationFrame, style calculation, layout, and paint to optimize performance.
